name: Mey
look: A sturdy eleven-year-old girl with wind-reddened cheeks and a tangle of red-brown hair, a grey wool shawl over a green dress, bare legs, wooden clogs and a crook taller than she is.
personality: Curious, brave and stubborn; asks 'why' about everything and believes in nothing she hasn't seen.
values: her father, the flock, finding things out
fears: the fog, losing her father on the hill
authority: Minds the flock when her father is away.
concerns: The fog comes down off the hill without warning; last spring her father was lost in it all night and they lost three ewes.

fog.text: When the fog comes down on the hill you can't tell one way from another; her father was lost in it last spring.
fog.line: When the fog comes down you can't tell up from down. Father was lost all night last spring.
fog.lead: The shepherds get lost on the hill when the fog comes down.

persuaded_by: seeing it work with her own eyes
style: Quick questions, one after another; sceptical, then delighted.

samples: Show me. I don't believe things I can't see.
Father says the fog's alive. I think it's just wet.
voice.habits: Asks why; wants to see things done; repeats new words.
voice.never: believes a thing just because she's told it
voice.greeting: Squints at you: 'You're not from the valley. Where are you from? Why?'

likes: clever things, stories of far places

npc_orrin_shepherd.text: her father; brave but too proud to ask for help

tasks.doing: counting the sheep in the fold

superstition.text: Mey would be thrilled by anything uncanny and tell the whole valley.
